title: Fat Worm Blows a Sparky
build: original Durell Software release, a tape image made with Ramsoft MakeTZX; a BASIC program loads a 190-byte turbo loader to $FAF2, which loads 49,000 bytes to $4000-$FF67 and returns to $EFD8

verification.note: the checker's own sample: 20 claims from facts.md (the nine marked live repeated live in the emulator), 10 names from symbols.json and 9 orientation facts, each traced in the bytes or run in a Z80 simulator; and, separately, a fixed-seed sample of 60 listing comments checked clause by clause with none wrong

failed.note: the first pass: 20 claims from facts.md, 10 names from symbols.json and the orientation facts, checked statically from listing.json; coverage and verify were then redone on claude-opus-5-5

credits.role: contributor (Spectrum Computing lists him; his role there is unstated)

tools.emulator: release ZEsarUX-13.0, ZEsarUX_macos-silicon-13.0.dmg; check-emulator 41 of 45 on 3 October 2026 (each of the four failures has a workaround in kit/skills/spectrum/tool-zesarux)
tools.disassembler: SkoolKit 10.1 (control file, snapshot tools, and its Z80 simulator through kit/spectrum/simulate.py)

model: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code: coverage, verify, minisite and retro, with nine annotation subagents on the same model and three checking subagents on claude-fable-5-1); deepseek-flash (Pi: orient, features, text, sweep, and a first coverage and verify that a maintainer's check refuted)

exclude: empty on the tape: the display list and the stack grow into it in play
empty on the tape: part of the frame buffer in play
the tape utility's copy of the ROM's cassette routines and the top of BASIC's memory: not the game's, never run by it, and not listed because it is the machine's ROM

regions: the live grid: the 5 by 5 cells round the worm
the board: 129 cells, each four link words and a list of 7-byte items
six object records copied into play every 512 passes
the object list's count, end pointer and first record
the worm's sections, its head, the fills' working words, counters and flags
the hand of the ending, as two scripts of four-sided shapes
pictures: sparks and discs in twenty sizes, explosions, legs, the disk, the Sputnik, the small Crawly, spindles
the counter display's two pictures, built in play
seven-segment masks and strokes, and ten digits for the panel
eight tiles for the halt screen
the sound list's pointer and counter, and six lists of click dividers
the tune: twelve pitch pairs, ten script addresses, ten scripts
the display list's head and a leftover record
the bottom panel's picture, copied to the screen once
